finding.claim: /fetch2 fetches any attacker-supplied http/https URL with no host or IP validation and returns the response body, enabling non-blind SSRF to loopback, private, and cloud-metadata addresses.

trace.note: is_http_url only checks urlparse(url).scheme in ('http','https'); no host/IP check
requests.get follows redirects (default) and returns body text to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist only. No hostname, IP-range, or port validation. Redirects are followed, so open redirects on public hosts can reach internal targets.

verdict.guard_found: none on the /fetch2 path. views.py:20 calls is_http_url, which validators.py:7 implements as a scheme-only check (urlparse(url).scheme in ("http","https")). No hostname, IP, or port check runs before the sink at views.py:22. The stronger is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18, which resolves the host and rejects private, loopback, link-local, and reserved addresses) is imported at views.py:4 and used only by /fetch at views.py:12, not by /fetch2.
verdict.reason: The url at views.py:19 is taken straight from the request query string, the only gate is the scheme-only is_http_url at views.py:20 / validators.py:7, and views.py:22 calls requests.get with default redirects enabled and returns the first 200 characters of the body, so an attacker can reach loopback, private, and metadata addresses (directly or via a redirect) and read the response.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the resolved IPs of the hostname but then performs its own independent DNS resolution when connecting, so an attacker-controlled DNS name can return a public IP for the check and a private IP for the request (DNS rebinding / TOCTOU).

trace.note: requires http/https scheme and non-empty hostname
socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, port) – first DNS resolution; result checked but not pinned
requests.get(url) performs a second, independent DNS resolution at connect time

finding.guards_checked: Resolve-and-reject on every returned address; allow_redirects=False blocks redirect-based bypass. Not checked: IP pinning between validation and connection; consistency between urllib.parse (validator) and urllib3 (client) URL parsing, including userinfo, backslash, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 edge cases, which was not verified by running code.

verdict.guard_found: validators.py:14-17 rejects private/loopback/link-local/reserved IPs from getaddrinfo, but this is an IP-range check, not a hostname membership, anchored match, or scheme-plus-host-allowlist, so it does not close the finding. No IP pinning exists between validators.py:14 and views.py:14. views.py:12 is the only call to is_safe_url before the request.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: views.py:11 takes the url query parameter from the request, views.py:12 calls is_safe_url, validators.py:14 resolves the hostname via getaddrinfo and only checks the returned IPs (validators.py:15-18), and views.py:14 calls requests.get(url), which performs its own resolution, so a DNS name that flips between a public and a private address defeats the check.
